Definition: from G1758; liable to (a condition, penalty or imputation):--in danger of, guilty of, subject to.
BiblicalUsage: Enochos is to be liable — guilty of, in danger of, subject to. Whoever eats the bread unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord in 1 Corinthians 11:27, whoever offends in one point is guilty of all in James 2:10, and the blasphemer against the Holy Ghost is in danger of eternal damnation in Mark 3:29. But Christ came to deliver those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage in Hebrews 2:15.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe guilt is real and total — one offence makes me guilty of all — and that is exactly why Christ's deliverance has to be total too. I hold that the fear of death held me in bondage until He who died set me free, and now no charge can hold me.
